spec_match.rationale: The GPU path never dispatches any compute shader — it creates and destroys an empty buffer and calls that 'setup ms' — so the advertised divergence sweep measures nothing; it also probes adapter.features for 'subgroup-uniformity', which is not a GPU feature (the spec surface is navigator.gpu.wgslLanguageFeatures 'subgroup_uniformity', exactly what the feature's conformance suite checks).

interactive.rationale: Sliders and Dispatch respond, but neither path produces an observable divergence effect: the divergence value is merely echoed back in the stats.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The blurb promises 'watch the verdict change' across a divergence sweep and a CPU-simulator fallback when WebGPU is unavailable — neither holds: the verdict depends only on feature presence, and the common adapter-null case shows a raw error instead of the promised CPU sim (CDP-verified: 'WebGPU init failed: no adapter', no stats).

edge_cases.rationale: The CPU fallback only triggers when navigator.gpu is entirely absent; adapter-null (headless, blocklisted GPUs — this environment) falls into the catch with no fallback, no stats, and no guidance.

references.rationale: No chromestatus.com/feature/<id> link — see-also lists only the two sibling concepts, breaking the invariant-3 self-heal contract.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite itself is well-targeted (wgslLanguageFeatures registry, subgroup_uniformity advertised, adapter subgroups, guarded requestDevice) and honestly reports 3 pass / 3 fail in this GPU-less pre-145 browser.

runtime_evidence.rationale: CDP-driven click reproduced the broken branch: 'WebGPU init failed: no adapter' with empty stats, contradicting both the on-page code comment and the index blurb; console otherwise clean.

telemetry_health.rationale: Server-injected /public/demo-telemetry.js verified in the served DOM.

design_system.rationale: Shared variables for controls, verdict, and stats.

accessibility.rationale: Range inputs are wrapped in labels, but the verdict/stats update silently — and the file ends with a malformed `</script role="button" tabindex=...>` closing tag, apparently a misapplied a11y patch.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-measured clean at 360x740 (scrollWidth 360); desktop verified via screenshot.

openQuestions.title: Actually dispatch the divergence workload
openQuestions.detail: The GPU path creates+destroys an empty buffer and reports 'setup ms'; no compute pipeline, no WGSL, no subgroup op ever runs, so the divergence slider changes nothing observable. Build the real benchmark: compile the shown WGSL (with/without enable subgroup_uniformity where advertised), dispatch across the divergence ratios, and read back timings or per-lane results so the verdict genuinely changes with the sweep.

openQuestions.title: Honour the promised CPU fallback on adapter-null
openQuestions.detail: requestAdapter() returning null (headless/blocklisted GPUs — reproduced here) throws into the catch and shows 'WebGPU init failed: no adapter' with no stats, while the blurb and in-page comment promise a CPU simulation. Route the no-adapter case into the existing CPU-sim branch.

openQuestions.title: Probe wgslLanguageFeatures, not a fictional adapter feature
openQuestions.detail: features.includes('subgroup-uniformity') can never be true — subgroup_uniformity is a WGSL language feature advertised via navigator.gpu.wgslLanguageFeatures (as the conformance suite asserts). Use that surface for the verdict.

openQuestions.title: Add the chromestatus link and fix the malformed closing script tag
openQuestions.detail: Invariant 3 requires chromestatus.com/feature/5673998232977408 on the page; also `</script role="button" tabindex="0" onkeydown=…>` is invalid HTML (attributes on a closing tag) and should be removed.

summary: Weakest page in the batch: the 'stress test' dispatches no compute work at all, the promised CPU fallback is skipped in the common adapter-null case (reproduced via CDP: raw 'no adapter' error), the probe targets a non-existent adapter feature name, the chromestatus link is missing, and the file ends in a malformed closing script tag. Needs a substantive in-place rebuild of its benchmark logic. Browser-verified with headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI (screenshot + DOM dump) and raw CDP (real click dispatch, console/network capture, 360x740 DPR3 mobile emulation) — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session. Chromium 141 predates Chrome 145, so v145-only API paths were validated on their fallback branches, not the new-API success path. The single failed fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet request is environmental (blocked host) and was not counted against any page.
